name: Functional Analysis

papers.title: A Perturbative Two-Eigenvalue Faber-Krahn Problem for the Gaussian Short-Time Fourier Transform
papers.abstract: We prove that, for every fixed s\in (0,\infty), the set of area s maximizing the weighted sum of the first two eigenvalues of the associated Toeplitz operators on the Fock space must be a disc, up to translations and sets of measure zero. To do so, we first prove the existence of maximizer sets. Then we show that every maximizer set must be a perturbation of a disc when the weight is sufficiently small. Finally, we use the vector-valued version of the analytic implicit function theorem and the inverse function theorem to conclude that the perturbation must vanish when the weight tends to zero.

papers.title: The Kalton--Peck space disproves Rubio de Francia's conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove that the classical complex Kalton--Peck space $Z_2$ is not isomorphic to $[X,H]_\theta$ for any UMD Banach space $X$, Hilbert space $H$, and $0<\theta<1$. Since $Z_2$ is UMD, this disproves Rubio de Francia's conjecture on intermediate UMD spaces. The proof combines the logarithmic block identity, a shift-commutator estimate on the interpolation strip, a unified obstruction in terms of reciprocal Hilbert norms, and Hahn--Banach with elementary convexity. It allows arbitrary compatible placements. We also realize $Z_2$ as a quotient of a closed subspace of an intermediate UMD space for every fixed interpolation parameter less than one.

papers.title: Sharpness of the Kadec'-type theorem for the union of intervals
papers.abstract: In this article, we establish the sharpness of a Kadec'-type theorem for finite unions of intervals admitting the integers as an orthonormal spectrum by constructing an explicit counterexample.

papers.title: Norm of the Generalized Hilbert Matrix Operator Between Some Spaces of Analytic Functions
papers.abstract: We study the generalized Hilbert operator \[ \mathcal H_bf(z)=\int_0^1\frac{(1-t)^b}{(1-tz)^{b+1}}f(t)\,dt, \qquad b>0, \] on several spaces of analytic functions in the unit disk. For logarithmically weighted Korenblum spaces, we obtain an exact supremum representation and a lower estimate for the norm of the mapping from $H_{\alpha,\log}^{\infty}$ to $H_\alpha^\infty$. We then establish two-sided estimates and characterize the boundedness range of $\mathcal H_b$ on the $\alpha$-Bloch spaces $\mathcal B^\alpha$. We also derive norm bounds for the mapping from $H^\infty$ into the endpoint Zygmund-type space $\Lambda_1^{1,*}$. Furthermore, we give a norm representation for $\mathcal H_b:H_\alpha^\infty\to\mathcal B^{\alpha+1}$ and identify a norm-attaining function. In particular, for $0<\alpha\leq2/3$, the norm is expressed explicitly in terms of a Beta function. Finally, we obtain an exact supremum representation of the norm of $\mathcal H_b$ on $H_{\alpha,\log}^{\infty}$, together with explicit norm estimates. Our results extend those of Hao et al. [J. Geom. Anal. 35 (2025), Paper No. 184] for the classical Hilbert matrix operator ($b=0$) to the generalized case $b>0$.

papers.title: A Non-Commutative Binomial Theorem, Extensions, and Applications
papers.abstract: This paper presents a matrix trace inequality analogous to the binomial theorem for reals: for Hermitian matrices $A$ and $B$, and a nonnegative even integer $k$ (and any nonnegative integer $k$ when $A, B$ are positive semi-definite), \[ \mathrm{tr}\bigl((A + B)^k\bigr) \le \sum_{\ell=0}^k \binom{k}{\ell} \mathrm{tr}\bigl(A^\ell B^{k-\ell}\bigr). \] The above natural inequality implies the classical Golden--Thompson inequality $\mathrm{tr}(e^{A + B}) \le \mathrm{tr}(e^A e^B)$. It also proves an extension, which can be used to show other new inequalities as well as give short proofs of inequalities such as the Schatten-$p$ two-point inequality for $p \ge 3$ and Hanner's inequality for $p \ge 3$. The main proof was discovered by Gemini Carbon within an agentic system.

papers.title: Nested Spherical Designs of Optimal Order
papers.abstract: Zheng and Zhuang [22] showed that a spherical $t_1$-design $Y$ with $|Y|=M\sim t_1^d$ points on the sphere $\mathbb{S}^d$ can be extended to a spherical $t$-design by adding points, with a total of order $t^{2d+1}$, and asked whether the optimal order $t^d$ is attainable. We keep their construction and improve the estimate of the pairing of the given points against polynomials of unit $L^1$-gradient norm. We prove that, if the given spherical $t_1$-design is upper regular at scale $t_1$ (in particular if it is well-separated; such a design exists by Bondarenko, Radchenko and Viazovska [6]), then for $d\ge2$, every $N\ge C(d,K)\,t^d$ suffices to admit a point set $X$ with $|X|=N$, for all $t_1<t$, such that the multiset union $X\uplus Y$ is a spherical $t$-design; in particular $|X\uplus Y|\le C(d,K)\,t^d$. The proof combines the design property, which removes the low frequencies exactly, with an $L^1$ Jackson-type estimate and a sampling inequality applied on dyadic frequency blocks. Upper regularity turns out to be automatic for nested spherical designs of optimal order; that is, every spherical $t_1$-design with $M\le C_M t_1^d$ points extends to a spherical $t$-design with $N+M\le C(d)\,C_M\,t^d$ (with $C_M\ge1$), uniformly in $t_1<t$, without any separation hypothesis. Some control of local multiplicity is necessary for an extension of optimal order. We also show that the estimate of the pairing functional cannot be improved within this method; that is, for every point set of at most $c\,t^d$ points it is at least of order $t^{d-1}$, and for upper regular designs it is of exactly this order. Finally, we treat finite chains of nested spherical designs, and on the circle we remove a logarithmic factor from the general estimate.

papers.title: The modulus of smoothness and \(\ell_p\)-generation
papers.abstract: Fabian, Godefroy, H\'ajek and Zizler [\emph{J. Funct. Anal.} \textbf{200} (2003), 301--323, Theorem~2] proved that at density \(\aleph_1\), generation by a space whose modulus of smoothness has power type \(p\), \(1<p\le 2\), is equivalent to \(\ell_p(\Gamma)\)-generation. We extend this equivalence to arbitrary density, with \(|\Gamma|=\dens X\), answering \mbox{Problem~291} of Guirao, Montesinos and Zizler [\emph{Open Problems in the Geometry and Analysis of Banach Spaces}, Springer, Cham (2016), p.~127]. The proof combines an upper \(\ell_p\)-estimate on successive projection differences with transfinite induction on density. We characterize generation by superreflexive spaces and by their \(\ell_2\)-sums, and obtain \(\ell_{\min\{r,2\}}\)-generation for closed subspaces of \(L^r(\mu)\), \(1<r<\infty\), including Hilbert generation for \(r\ge 2\).

papers.title: Pettis integrability of $L^1$-functions in locally convex spaces
papers.abstract: In this article, for a Hausdorff locally convex space $E$, we investigate conditions under which every Lusin-measurable $L^1$-function $\gamma:[0,1]\to E$ is Pettis integrable. We show that this property on $E$ is local and equivalent to $E$ being absolutely summable and satisfying the metric convex compactness property. Via examples, we show that these two properties are independent. Moreover, we establish sufficient conditions, for a Lusin-measurable weakly integrable function with values in the topological dual $E'$, to be Gelfand integrable.

papers.title: Exact sequences of regular LF-spaces
papers.abstract: We show that the category of regular LF-spaces has all kernels but, unlike the category of regular LB-spaces, does not have all cokernels. Its topological exact structure, maximal exact structure and maximal deflation-exact structure form a strictly increasing chain of proper subclasses of the class of all kernel-cokernel pairs. To the best of the authors' knowledge, regular LF-spaces in particular provide the first natural example of a category that has all kernels but is not preabelian and whose maximal deflation-exact structure is neither two-sided exact nor equal to the class of all kernel-cokernel pairs.

papers.title: Pietsch's favourite problem on singular traces
papers.abstract: In 2023, A. Pietsch formulated twenty-seven open problems concerning traces on operator ideals. We give an affirmative answer to Problem 16, which Pietsch singled out as his personal favourite, by constructing a nonzero bounded singular spectral trace on the weak Weyl ideal over the class of all Banach spaces.

papers.title: Uniqueness Sequences in the Bargmann-Fock Space
papers.abstract: We show that a locally finite sequence with prescribed multiplicities is a uniqueness sequence in the Bargmann-Fock space if and only if a variational supremum involving Jensen potentials and Gaussian relative entropy is infinite. The proof combines exact subharmonic duality with holomorphic realization at the original Gaussian weight. Restricting the supremum to radial tests yields a necessary and sufficient integral criterion for locally finite unions of pairwise disjoint regular rotation orbits satisfying a bounded-overlap condition. For a planar lattice containing the origin and having fundamental area $\pi$, changing only the arguments of its nonzero points yields a uniqueness sequence provided that the resulting points are pairwise distinct. In particular, independently and uniformly rotating the nonzero points of the critical square lattice yields an almost surely complete system of coherent states. Finally, we reduce the general criterion to countably many polynomial tests and give finite approximations to each test score with explicit error bounds.

papers.title: Cyclic polynomials in mixed-weighted Dirichlet-type spaces
papers.abstract: For $\boldsymbol{\alpha}=(\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\alpha_3)\in\mathbb R^3$, we investigate cyclic polynomials in the mixed-weighted Dirichlet-type space $\mathscr{D}_{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}$ of holomorphic functions $f(z_1,z_2)=\sum_{m,n\geq0}a_{m,n}z_1^mz_2^n$ on the unit bidisk satisfying $$ \sum_{m,n\geq0}|a_{m,n}|^2 (m+1)^{\alpha_1}(n+1)^{\alpha_2} (m+n+1)^{\alpha_3}<\infty. $$ We give a complete characterization of cyclic polynomials in terms of their zero sets and the parameters $\alpha_1,\alpha_2,\alpha_3$. Our results extend previously known characterizations for anisotropic and total-degree Dirichlet-type spaces on the unit bidisk.

papers.title: A Garnett--Jones estimate for matrix weights
papers.abstract: For an \(N\times N\) matrix \(A_p\) weight \(W\) on an averaging basis, set \(M_p=\max\{1,p-1\}\), \(1\leq p<\infty\). At rate \(1/M_p\), the operator-norm exponential moment of \(\log W\) centered on each basis set is bounded by \(2[W]_{\mathbf A_p}^{1/M_p}\). With scalar Garnett--Jones constant \(G\), the BMO distance from \(\log W\) to bounded Hermitian functions is at most \((2N^2-N)GM_p\), uniformly in the characteristic. Power weights on intervals show the sharp order in \(p\). Conversely, a uniform distance bound for scalar \(A_2\) logarithms gives the scalar property with the same constant. Under a uniform small-BMO condition this is equivalent to scalar \(A_2\) decomposition. The estimates apply to cubes and axis-parallel rectangles on \(\R^d\) and \(\T^d\). For rectangles with \(d>1\), the scalar quadratic estimate bounds the distance by \(\sqrt{2N^2-N}\,C_d M_p\), where \(C_d\) depends only on \(d\). The rectangular BMO distance is comparable to the critical exponential scale.

papers.title: Characterisations of symmetric Birkhoff--James orthogonality via numerical ranges
papers.abstract: Birkhoff-James orthogonality in a normed space is in general not symmetric. For a complex Banach space $\mathscr{X}$ of dimension at least $2$, we prove that the following assertions are equivalent: Birkhoff-James orthogonality in $\mathscr{X}$ is symmetric; the spatial numerical range of every operator on $\mathscr{X}$ coincides with its reverse numerical range, defined by reversing the orthogonality; $\mathscr{X}$ has the simultaneous zero inclusion property, that is, $0$ lies in the closure of the numerical range of an invertible operator exactly when it lies in that of its inverse; $\mathcal{B}(\mathscr{X})$ has the analogous property for the algebra numerical range; and a simple inequality for supporting functionals holds. This confirms a conjecture of Ghosh. We also introduce the asymmetry constant $R(\mathscr{X})\in[1,2]$, as the supremum of the norms of the projections $I-x\otimes\xi$, where $x$ is a unit vector and $\xi$ is a supporting functional at $x$. We show that $R(\mathscr{X})^{-1}$ is the radius of the largest ball around the identity on which the simultaneous zero inclusion property holds, and that every number in $[1,2]$ is the asymmetry constant of some two-dimensional $\ell^p$ space.

papers.title: The positive-sphere variant of Tingley's problem for $C^1([0,1])$
papers.abstract: Let $C^1([0,1])$ be endowed with the norm $\|f\|=\|f\|_\infty+\|f'\|_\infty$, and let $S(C^1([0,1]))^+$ be the part of its unit sphere consisting of nonnegative, nondecreasing functions. We prove that every surjective isometry of $S(C^1([0,1]))^+$ is the identity and has a unique surjective real-linear isometric extension to $C^1([0,1])$.

papers.title: Linearization of completely Lipschitz functions
papers.abstract: We develop a linearization theory for completely Lipschitz mappings between operator spaces. Motivated by the classical theory of Lipschitz-free spaces, we introduce a completely Lipschitz-free space and show that completely Lipschitz mappings admit a canonical linearization as completely bounded operators on this space. We provide several equivalent descriptions of this operator space, extending to the noncommutative setting the classical constructions of Arens--Eells, de Leeuw, and Dixmier--Ng. In particular, we obtain a molecular description, a quotient representation of an operator $\ell_1$-space, and a realization as the closed linear span of evaluation functionals. Our framework applies over both the real and complex scalar fields; in the real case, we first establish some operator space results needed to carry out the constructions. We also show that our notion of completely Lipschitz mapping encompasses the previously introduced extensions of Lipschitz mappings to operator spaces. These results provide a unified framework for studying Lipschitz phenomena in the setting of operator spaces and establish the corresponding free operator spaces as a natural tool for their linearization.

papers.title: A Rellich-type inequality for the sphere
papers.abstract: We prove a Rellich-type inequality of the form $$\int |(\Delta + 1)u|^2dx \geq C_d \int \frac{|u|^2}{(1 - |x|^2)^2}dx $$ for smooth functions $u$ compactly supported in the unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^d$ for $d \geq 1$. The obtained constant is asymptotically sharp up to the first three orders, as $d \rightarrow \infty$. We also show that in the complement of the ball, the inequality holds only in dimension one, and does not hold true with a positive $C_d>0$ for $d \geq 2$. The motivation is that if $\hat{u}$ denotes the Fourier transform of $u$, then the inequality is associated with the uncertainty principle $$ \left(\int |u|^2dx\right)^2 \lesssim \int (1-|x|^2)^2|u|^2dx \int (1 - |\xi|^2)^2|\hat{u}|^2 d\xi,$$ which says that a function cannot be simultaneously concentrated on a sphere in both space and frequency. This is in analogy with the classical Hardy inequality together with the Heisenberg uncertainty principle.

papers.title: Separable models of an NIP Banach space theory
papers.abstract: Let $Y$ be the renorming of $\ell_2(\mathbb N)\oplus_2\ell_2(\mathbb N)$ with norm $(h^2+q^2)^{1/2}$, where $h$ is the Hilbert norm and $q(u,v)=\sup_{i<j}|u_i+v_j|$. We prove that the unstable theory $\operatorname{Th}(Y)$ is NIP in the pure Banach language. We recover the index order from the Banach norm and classify the continuum many separable models up to surjective linear isometry. The invariants are the order type of a countable model of $\operatorname{Th}(\mathbb N,<)$ and the dimension of a separable Hilbert summand. Every such pair occurs. We describe all elementary embeddings between these models. The bounded norm types over a separable model are separable in the uniform metric exactly when its index order contains no copy of $(\mathbb Q,<)$.

papers.title: On Grokking and the Dynamics of Generalization
papers.abstract: We extend the signal-channel theory of grokking introduced by Litman and Guo by relating training dissipation and evaluation transfer to population risk. For preconditioned gradient flows with time-dependent kernels, we distinguish two sources of limited evaluation visibility, namely small cumulative dissipation and weak transfer. We obtain quantitative bounds for task visibility and establish their stability under signal filtering and changes of evaluation distribution. We describe how task directions enter the effective signal channel through spectral activation or transport. We establish necessary and sufficient conditions for the transferred signal to decrease squared population risk and derive classification error bounds under margin assumptions. These results yield sufficient conditions for the same training trajectory to generalize under one evaluation distribution while failing under another. We show that differences in spectral learning rates can produce arbitrarily long delays between low training loss and low population risk. By relating classification accuracy to the distribution of margin crossing times, we construct a family of gradient flows in which the generalization delay tends to infinity, while both the duration of the transition from zero to full accuracy and the corresponding variation of population risk tend to zero. These phenomena occur without feature evolution during training. Finally, we prove that the occurrence and timing of generalization cannot generally be inferred from training dynamics alone, but depend on the geometry of evaluation transfer and its relation to the target.

papers.title: Parallel sums of nilpotent elements: exact realization and structured eigenvalue splitting
papers.abstract: We prove that, over every infinite field and for $m\ge2$, the parallel sums $N(N+C)^{-1}C$ of nilpotent $m\times m$ inputs with invertible sum are exactly the matrices of nullity at least two. Every positive split of the target nullity between the input kernels is realizable. Over $\mathbb{C}$, we determine the paired derivative image and characterize universal full matrix cancellation at nonzero residues. For analytic input paths, nilpotence is required only at the base. An adjugate identity forces the last two characteristic coefficients to be $O(\varepsilon^2)$, yielding sharp bounds $O(|\varepsilon|^{2/3})$ at nonzero three-dimensional nilpotent residues and $O(|\varepsilon|^{1/(m-2)})$ at nilpotent residues for $m\ge4$. At every base with residue of type $[m-1,1]$, $m\ge4$, we prove a generic splitting law, also with fixed input sum. For $m\ge5$, it has $m-2$ roots on the scale $|\varepsilon|^{1/(m-2)}$ and two on the scale $|\varepsilon|^{1/2}$, separating the largest-root and spectral-gap scales. A separate sharpness family keeps both inputs nilpotent and two roots zero. At the nonzero nilpotent three-dimensional boundary, a finite coefficient criterion computes the splitting orders for each exceptional affine fixed-sum direction. For each such path, the punctured spectral gap is at least $c|\varepsilon|^3$ near zero for some $c>0$, and the exponent is optimal over this class. Over a nonzero unital ring with $2$ invertible, we construct two $3\times3$ matrix inputs, each of nilpotency index exactly three, with invertible sum. In the complex unital Banach case, the residue has spectrum ${0}\cup\tfrac12\sigma(Q)$ for every coefficient $Q$. With the common core allowed to vary, a complex matrix is a finite-Drazin Hua output if and only if its nullity is not one.

papers.title: Weak monotonicity, Critical exponents, and Gagliardo-Nirenberg inequalities on weighted graphs
papers.abstract: We study weak monotonicity of heat kernel and ball averaged functionals on weighted graphs, and the associated critical exponents. Under sub-Gaussian heat kernel estimates, weak Bakry-\'Emery estimates for the semigroup are proved, with explicit values of the H\"older regularity exponent in the strongly recurrent case. Applications of the theory include Gagliardo-Nirenberg, Sobolev, Nash and isoperimetric inequalities on strongly recurrent graphs and their products.

papers.title: A Characterization of Douglas Weights
papers.abstract: A weight $\omega$ on the unit disc is a \emph{Douglas weight} if the $\omega$-energy of the Poisson extension of every Lipschitz function $f$ on the unit circle equals $\iint|f(\zeta)-f(\lambda)|^2\,d\J_\omega$ for some positive symmetric measure $\J_\omega$ off the diagonal. For radial weights, we show that this holds if and only if \[ j_\omega(\theta) = \int_0^1 \frac{\omega(r)}{r}\, \partial_\theta^2 P(r^2,\theta)\,dr \geq 0, \qquad 0<\theta\leq\pi, \] where $P(x,\theta)$ denotes the Poisson kernel. We also obtain a complete characterization of the Douglas weights among arbitrary weights. The class of Douglas weights strictly contains the nonnegative superharmonic weights, and we give examples that are neither superharmonic nor subharmonic.

papers.title: Extremals and Normalized Solutions for a Critical Weighted Choquard Equation
papers.abstract: We study normalized solutions to the weighted Choquard equation \[ \left\{ \begin{aligned} -\operatorname{div}(|x|^{-2a}\nabla u) &=\lambda |x|^{-2a}u+\beta |x|^{-bq}|u|^{q-2}u\\ &\quad+|x|^{-bp} \left( \int_{\mathbb R^N} \frac{|u(y)|^p}{|x-y|^{\mu}|y|^{bp}}\,dy \right) |u|^{p-2}u &&\text{in }\mathbb R^N,\\ \int_{\mathbb R^N}|x|^{-2a}u^2\,dx&=\rho^2, \end{aligned} \right. \] where $N\ge3$, $a<(N-2)/2$, $a<b<a+1$, $2<q<2^\sharp$, $0<\mu<N$, $p=(2N-\mu)/(N-2d)$ is the upper Stein--Weiss critical exponent, $d=1-b+a$, $2^\sharp=2N/(N-2-2a+2b)$, $\rho>0$ is prescribed, $\beta>0$, and $\lambda\in\mathbb R$ is an unknown Lagrange multiplier. Assuming $p>2$, we establish existence and multiplicity of normalized solutions in different mass regimes, including negative-energy ground states for small $\beta$ and positive-energy second solutions under suitable assumptions, as well as ground states in the mass-critical and mass-supercritical cases under explicit conditions

papers.title: A Joint Functional Central Limit Theorem for the $L^p$-Norm Profile of Random Littlewood Polynomials
papers.abstract: For a random Littlewood polynomial $q_n(z)=\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}\varepsilon_jz^j$ with independent Rademacher coefficients, let $S_n(\theta)=|q_n(e^{i\theta})|^2/n$ be its normalized angular intensity. Its positive moments $T_n^{(p)}=\|q_n\|_p^p/n^{p/2}$ form the moment profile of the intensity distribution under normalized arc measure on the unit circle. We prove a joint functional central limit theorem for this profile. For $p$ in a compact interval $K\subset(0,\infty)$ and logarithmic time $n=\lfloor Ne^t\rfloor$, $t\in[-T,T]$, the piecewise linear interpolations of $\sqrt n(T_n^{(p)}-\Gamma(1+p/2))$ converge to a Gaussian field $G(p,t)$ in $C(K\times[-T,T])$. The corresponding step processes converge in $D([-T,T];C(K))$ with the Skorokhod $J_1$-topology. The limit has the representation $G(p,t)=\sum_{a=2}^{\infty}c_a(p)G^{(a)}(t)$, where $c_a(p)$ are the ordinary Laguerre coefficients of $x^{p/2}$, with $L_a(0)=1$. The independent centered stationary Gaussian modes have covariance $\mathrm{Cov}(G^{(a)}(s),G^{(a)}(t))=2V_a e^{-(a-1/2)|t-s|}$, where $V_a$ is the squared $L^2$-norm of the density of the sum of $a$ independent uniform random variables on $[0,1]$. We also obtain the functional limit theorem for $\|q_n\|_p/\sqrt n$ and identify its joint covariance. At $p=4$, we recover the known scalar autocorrelation fluctuation law and identify its dependence across nested lengths. Finite-mode convergence follows from the multivariate functional de Jong theorem after model-specific variance, influence, and fourth-moment calculations. Maximal estimates control the infinite Laguerre tail and its exponent derivative uniformly over nested lengths.

papers.title: Measurable equidecomposability and the Banach--Ruziewicz problem over locally compact non-Archimedean valued fields
papers.abstract: We prove a measurable analogue of the Banach--Tarski paradox over locally compact non-Archimedean valued fields. Let $\mathbb K$ be the completion of a number field at a non-Archimedean place (e.g., $\mathbb K=\mathbb Q_p$) and $n\ge 2$. Then any two bounded Haar measurable subsets of $\mathbb K^n$ with nonempty interior and equal Haar measure can be cut into finitely many Haar measurable pieces and rearranged into each other by elements of a certain countable group $\Gamma$ of affine isometries. We also show that the Haar measure is, up to a constant factor, the unique nonzero finitely additive $\Gamma$-invariant measure on the bounded Haar measurable subsets of $\mathbb K^n$, which solves a $p$-adic version of the Banach--Ruziewicz problem. Both results follow from the fact that the action of $\Gamma$ on $\mathbb K^n$ is expanding, a property closely related to the spectral gap. For $n=1$ and arbitrary characteristic, we obtain analogous results when the residue field is not prime, using a countable group of isometries that are not necessarily affine.

papers.title: Generic bi-stochastic semigroups are flows
papers.abstract: We demonstrate genericity wrt. the weak polynomial topology of the space $\mathrm{Aut}(X, \mu)$ of invertible measure-preserving transformations within the space of bi-stochastic operators over $L^{2}(X, \mu)$ for standard probability spaces $(X, \mu)$. This improves upon the approximation and residuality results established by Brown [4] and Kim [26] (cf. also [16]). We make crucial use of a reformulation of the Birkhoff--von Neumann theorem [2, 43] due to Kim for bi-stochastic operators over infinite dimensional Hilbert spaces. This enables the construction of stochastic processes, via which dilations and thereby $\mathrm{PW}$-approximations may be obtained. In a similar fashion, we demonstrate the weak-genericity of weakly-continuous measure-preserving flows on $(X, \mu)$ within the space of $\mathcal{C}_{0}$-semigroups of bi-stochastic operators on $L^{2}(X, \mu)$. To achieve this, we make use of random measures (viz. Poisson point processes) and build on our discrete-time result. This complements recent advances in ergodic theory due to Furlong on the genericity of measure-preserving flows in the space of measure-preserving semi-flows.

papers.title: The truncated $\mathbb{Z}-$moment problem
papers.abstract: We study the truncated moment problem on the one-dimensional full integer lattice $\mathbb{Z}$, seeking necessary and sufficient conditions for a prescribed sequence of $n$ real numbers to be $\mathbb{Z}-$representable, i.e. to be the sequence of the first $n$ moments of a probability measure supported on $\mathbb{Z}$. Building on the approach developed in 2017 in Infusino et al. for the truncated moment problem on the non-negative integers, we establish a complete characterization of $\mathbb{Z}-$representable sequences for every truncation order $n$. From this result, we derive an inductive and computable $\mathbb{Z}-$representability criterion. More generally, we also investigate the relationship between the truncated $\mathbb{Z}-$moment problem and the truncated Hamburger moment problem, seen as its continuous counterpart.
